Gaussian windows and analytic directions

Original exposition and proofs: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), October 2026. CC0.

A Gaussian centered at a complex point records both position and covector direction. Its unrestricted growth is known exactly. A strict exponential improvement near one complex center is equivalent to absence of the corresponding analytic singularity. We prove this for every compactly supported hyperfunction, without a distributional order bound. The main steps are moving a carrier, recovering a source from its Gaussian windows, and separating the directions of a holomorphic boundary.

We use complex-linear pairings, the Fourier sign , and . Dimension is positive. A square is complex bilinear; is not. Surface measure on is unnormalized; in dimension one it assigns mass one to each of .

The every-neighborhood bounds and germ action of analytic functionals are proved in Analytic tests and real carriers, Theorems 1 and 5. Hyperfunctions from local analytic sources, Proposition 4 and the extension theorem, identifies compactly supported hyperfunctions with analytic functionals and gives closure-supported extensions from bounded opens. We use the contour carrier, angular continuity, analytic regularity and holomorphic-side theorems in Holomorphic boundary values without growth bounds, Lemma 1, Proposition 2 and Theorems 3–7. The exact angular wavefront bound and conic splitting are Directional splitting and holomorphic compatibility, Lemma 1 and Theorem 2.

Fourier inversion and its constants are proved in the Schwartz and Fourier foundation, F1–F5; polar integration is the angular foundation, A4–A5. The Cauchy foundation, CX7–CX11 and CMI6–CMI8, supplies derivative estimates and real-to-complex identity. Cutoffs, finite covers and limiting integrals use the supplied metric foundation, Sections 12–13, and integration foundation, Sections 15–16.

Corollary 5 (local representatives give the same criterion). If two compact analytic functionals agree on a real neighborhood of , their Gaussian tests give the same answer in (G29), for every . Hence the criterion defines analytic regularity for an arbitrary hyperfunction by taking any compact local representative.
